issue_context.title: roachtest: include link to testeng grafana in issue posts
issue_context.body:
This is a wishlist feature request: When a roachtest fails and its metrics were reported to the testeng grafana instance, it would be very helpful in triaging if the posted GitHub issue could include a link to the grafana with the relevant cluster and test timeframe selected. As an example, a failure from a disk stall could easily be determined just by looking at the fsync latency.

Jira issue: CRDB-29261
comments: Good idea! I wish the test-eng data lived on CentMon so we could use the standard set of Investigation Dashboards for it, too.

Some breadcrumbs. Roachtest's entry point for posting issues is here

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/3266026f39ef3587515af2cf17a6635d88ea6949/pkg/cmd/roachtest/github.go#L215-L221

We'd probably put this link in the `HelpCommand`:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/3266026f39ef3587515af2cf17a6635d88ea6949/pkg/cmd/roachtest/github.go#L195-L204

So basically the task is to write code that generates the link

```
https://grafana.testeng.crdb.io/d/crdb-console/crdb-console-overview?orgId=1&from=<FROMEPOCHSECONDS>&to=<TOEPOCHSECONDS>&var-cluster=<CLUSTERNAME>
```

and renders it inline via `HelpCommandAsLink`.

While we're here, it might be useful to pull out the `HelpCommand` impl into a free-standing function and to write unit tests for it (perhaps a small one using `echotest`)[^1].

[^1]: [here's an example of how echotest works](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/227fbe78ba7e96ce15cd57b22f9dbd965700b854/pkg/kv/kvserver/concurrency/poison/error_test.go#L29-L39).

One small trailer of an idea, instead of hard-linking the test-eng grafana, we could use a vanity URL instead using https://go.crdb.dev/, which allows rewrites. I just set one up:

https://go.crdb.dev/p/roachfana/silvano-cluster/1689957243817/1689957733137

So the link is `https://go.crdb.dev/p/roachfana/<clustername>/<fromts>/<tots>`.

review_comments: minor: why enumerate all parameters instead of just passing `(t Test, message string)`?

ah so the `start` and `end` times belong to `*testImpl`; thus, those had to be passed in.

- the other thought was to change the `test.Test` type to `*testImpl` since `createPostRequest` only gets used with arguments of type `*testImpl` currently.
    - however, the conclusion to this (after speaking with Tobias) is that `*testImpl` is a "grab bag of stuff" that would lead to a more difficult time testing.
    
as for the `name` and `spec` fields, i did this since the function itself didn't seem to specifically need a `Test` other than to get the `name` and the `spec` (since t.Fatalf is now replaced). i am open to discuss this!

i believe this is one more parameter in the function signature than i promised Tobias...
Make sense - I tend not to like functions with long arg lists.
